ME011-C7P2: The October 1 land-travel guidance permitted departure subject to a two-week stay abroad, with stated commuter/medical exceptions. It bounds the former blanket citizen departure prohibition without proving uniform physical enforcement or the first actual crossing date.

Freight remains outside these passenger phases. This record is distinct from the January 2021 closure and does not assume the later direct Saudi road already operated. Numeric operational duration remains withheld.

The October 4 MEED chronology described ordinary land travel as still closed except for special permits, goods and medical supplies. This reinforces the distinction between the October 1 conditional guidance and proof of unrestricted operation. The July 14 citizen-travel easing explicitly concerned airports and cannot date land reopening.

The January and February dates describe successive ordered policy versions, not a measured continuous closure. January 25 and February 1/8 were scheduled expiry dates, not observed reopening. The February continuation included truck and citizen-return exceptions. June 2 permitted specified cross-border workers. UAE-to-Oman passenger admission was authorized from September 1, 2021, and reporting on September 15 documents actual Emirati tourist arrivals. This supplies a scoped ended-by bound. The first reopening at every outlet, other passenger cohorts, Yemen routes and continuous January–September operation remain unestablished.

The February 10 decision gives the citizen-return deadline as 12 am on Sunday, 21 February 2021; the Arabic text also says the twelfth hour of Sunday morning. The former 10:00 clock entry was unsupported and is corrected to midnight. This deadline ended an exception, not the land closure.

notes.qualification: NA012-C7P1 records an August 5, 2024 observation that Ghadames–Debdeb remained closed to citizen travel for security reasons on the Libyan side. LANA’s August 3, 2023 report also distinguishes passenger reopening preparations from existing commercial traffic. Anadolu identifies May 2014 as Ghadames–Debdeb’s historical closure, while its 2011 closure and 2015 local exceptions concern Tin Al Koum and Tarat; LANA’s broad frontier summary is less gate-specific. These historical accounts do not establish one continuous Ghadames passenger interval: a June 2020 contemporary report describes limited exceptional departures and stranded Libyans awaiting further permission. The planned December 12, 2023 reopening was expressly postponed. Indexed regional reporting dated August 5, 2026 still describes preparations with no announced reopening date, not observed gate-level passage. The repeated descriptions of an ordinary passenger restriction pending reopening in August and December 2023 and still closed in August 2024 support a restriction longer than 24 hours, independently of the unknown exact onset. Authorized exceptional departures do not contradict the non-exempt passenger restriction. First ordinary passenger restoration, exact onset of the present spell and continuous numeric duration remain unresolved.

Earlier partial permission — 2022-06-18
Contemporary Fars reporting records Iraqi permission for visa-free entry by Iranian pilgrims in approved Hajj and Pilgrimage Organization caravans. June 19 reporting identifies Mehran and Shalamcheh, a 2,500-person daily initial quota, and registration ahead of the first planned departures. This is a permission date, not observed first traffic. Individual visa-free travel remained excluded; earlier visa/authorization holders could pass. A July 25 official account subsequently announced individual or group pilgrimage access through Mehran and Shalamcheh for Muharram, with passport and vaccination requirements.

Separate later permission observation — by 2022-08-31
A named Iranian deputy interior minister reported that both countries’ land borders had reopened for Arbaeen processions, specifically naming Mehran and Shalamcheh. This bounds blanket exclusion for that eligible pilgrim group only; it is not the exact repeal date of Iraq’s 2020 policy or a statement about all non-Iraqi passengers.
